note: Augros Chapter 5 ↔ Euclid Elements Book V. Magnitudes and proportion (Eudoxus).

pairs.note: Invertendo: if A:B = C:D then B:A = D:C. Euclid lists inverse ratio as V.Def.13; it is not a numbered proposition.

pairs.euclidTitle: Ratios the same with the same ratio are the same with one another

pairs.note: A ratio cannot be both greater and less than another — trichotomy, used throughout Book V.
If some equimultiples of the terms are equal in pairs, the four quantities are proportional. Close to the converse of V.4.

pairs.euclidTitle: Equals have the same ratio to the same

pairs.note: Construction of equimultiples that witness A > B against a third magnitude C — the engine of V.8.

pairs.euclidTitle: The greater has a greater ratio to the same

pairs.note: A:B > C:D when C < A and D > B.

pairs.euclidTitle: Magnitudes having the same ratio to the same are equal
That which has the greater ratio is greater
If A:B = C:D and A > C then B > D
Parts have the same ratio as similar multiples
As one of the antecedents is to one of the consequents, so are all the antecedents to all the consequents

euclidOnly.euclidTitle: If A:B = C:D and C:D > E:F then A:B > E:F
As the whole to the whole, so the remainder to the remainder
Adding proportions with a common second/fourth
The sum of the greatest and least exceeds the sum of the other two
